name: Ornate Pitta
rangeDescription: Lombok, sumbawa, flores, adonara, lomblen, and alor islands
description: A typical pitta: plump, short-tailed, long-legged, and primarily terrestrial (sometimes perches up to call). Bright green above with electric blue shoulder patch and rump and black head with conspicuous pale brow.

name: Tawny-crested Tanager
rangeDescription: Tropical eastern honduras to western ecuador; isla gorgona (off colombia)
description: Male is all black with a conspicuous orangey crest. Female is confusing: dark dull brown, with typical stout tanager bill.

name: Blackish-blue Seedeater
rangeDescription: Locally from southeastern paraguay to eastern brazil and northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Compact finch with a small head and short, gray conical bill. Found in the understory of forests and woodlands with bamboo.

name: Black-breasted Buttonquail
rangeDescription: Coastal eastern australia (southeastern queensland and northern new south wales)
description: Dark buttonquail of forested areas with dense layers of leaf litter in southeastern Queensland. Heavily patterned, with pale and dark mark markings below.

name: White-winged Tapaculo
rangeDescription: East slope of the andes of northern peru (amazonas, south of the río marañón, to huánuco, north of the río huallaga)
description: Described to science in 2020, this tapaculo was long overlooked due to its similarity with other species. It ranges in high elevation cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes in northern and central Peru.

name: Semicollared Hawk
rangeDescription: Mountains of colombia to southwestern venezuela, ecuador, and southern peru
description: Tiny, rare hawk of mid-elevation cloud forest. Black upperparts and crown are separated by white band on back of neck, which can be indistinct and hard to see in the field.

name: White-browed Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southeastern brazil to northeastern argentina and eastern paraguay
description: Medium-sized woodpecker found in both montane and lowland humid forests. Olive-green above and barred below with a yellow throat.

name: Red-flanked Bluetail
rangeDescription: Breeds from finland and northern russia eastward to mongolia, northeastern china, korea, and japan; resident in japan (except for hokkaido), otherwise winters to southern china, taiwan, indochina, myanmar, and thailand
description: Beautiful adult male is shimmering sky-blue above and pale below, with orange sides and a small white eyebrow. Female and juvenile are more subdued, but still have the rufous flanks and blue tail.

name: Yellow-billed Giant-Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Fiji (taveuni and vanua levu)
description: A very large, robust honeyeater. Entirely drab grayish-olive, with yellowish wings and tail and a bright yellow bill and eye-ring.

name: Prince Henry's Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Semiarid montane scrub of western china (southwestern xinjiang and southeastern tibet)
description: Handsome laughingthrush endemic to the southeastern Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau and its adjacent Himalayan foothills. Gray overall, with a dark rust-colored face, slate-blue-and-orange wing panels, and a bright white “moustache.” An adaptable species, occurring in and around human habitation, as well as naturally-occurring brushy and scrubby areas such as forest edges and gulches.

name: White-fronted Swift
rangeDescription: Mountains of southwestern mexico (jalisco, guerrero, and michoacán)
description: Poorly known and rarely seen medium-sized swift. Very local in west Mexico and very rarely identified in the field.

name: Half-collared Sparrow
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (rio de janeiro to rio grande do sul)
description: Boldly-patterned sparrow found in the understory of humid forest and second growth; usually difficult to see. Note the bicolored bill (black above and bright yellow below) and black patches on either side of the breast.

name: Wood Thrush
rangeDescription: Breeds eastern north america; winters southern texas to panama
description: Boldly patterned thrush is bright rusty-brown above with black spots on the white belly. Smaller than a robin, but larger than Hermit Thrush.

name: Elegant Tern
rangeDescription: Southern california to western mexico (nayarit); winters guatemala to chile
description: Long-billed tern of the Pacific coast, from the U.S. to Chile.

name: Rock Earthcreeper
rangeDescription: Andes of western bolivia to northwestern argentina and adjacent northern chile
description: Common earthcreeper of wooded and shrubby parts of the high Andes and Altiplano from NW Argentina to N Bolivia, including ravines and Polylepis woodland. Despite its name, prefers low vegetation, and is generally absent from open desert areas (where Straight-billed Earthcreeper is more common).

name: Black-capped Bulbul
rangeDescription: Sri lanka
description: Medium-sized greenish bird with a bright yellow underside and black head. Occurs in a variety of habitats, wherever there are trees, including forest, open woodlands, and gardens, in the lowlands and foothills.

name: Piping Crow
rangeDescription: Central and southern sulawesi, muna, and buton islands
description: A distinctive black-and-white crow that occurs within the canopy of hill and mountain forest on Sulawesi and satellite islands. White parts of adults are duller on juveniles.

name: Luapula Cisticola
rangeDescription: Northern and northeastern namibia, eastern angola, southeastern democratic republic of the congo, zambia (except northeastern), northern botswana, and northwestern zimbabwe
description: Relatively colorful, mid-sized, long-tailed cisticola. Note the brown back with thick black streaks, rufous on the wing and cap, and pale underparts.

name: Blue-billed Black-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil to uruguay, eastern paraguay, and northeastern argentina
description: Large, crestless flycatcher found along the borders of humid forests and in gallery forests, often close to water. Male is mostly glossy black, while females are brown above with a cinnamon rump and buffy below with heavy brown streaks.

name: Mouse-gray Flycatcher
rangeDescription: West of the andes in southwestern colombia, western ecuador, and northwestern peru (southward to southwestern cajamarca)
description: Small, dull-colored flycatcher fond of lightly wooded areas, dry savanna, and forest edge. Its brownish-gray plumage, streaky breast, and buffy wingbars separate it from other similar species.
